intro: Property managers verify income by collecting and cross-referencing documents like pay stubs, bank statements, and tax returns against the applicant's stated employment. blocks.text: The manual burden of income verification

Verifying income is one of the most time-consuming parts of the leasing process. You often receive PDFs, images, or even screenshots of bank accounts. Each one needs a human eye to ensure the numbers match the application. On a Mac, this often means opening files in Preview, checking the dates, and verifying the employer contact information.
How to verify income using standard Mac tools

You do not need expensive software to start a basic verification workflow. Use Finder to create a folder structure for each applicant. Use Preview to open PDF pay stubs. If you need to highlight specific values for your audit trail, use the Markup toolbar in Preview. Press ⌘ + ⇧ + A to open the tools. You can draw a box around the net income to make it easy to see later.

items: Create a folder in Finder for the applicant name.
Save all received documents into this folder immediately.
Use the Highlight tool to mark the income amount.
Check the document date to ensure it is within the last 30 to 60 days.

blocks.text: Always follow your local laws and your employer's data privacy policy when handling sensitive tenant information. Never store unencrypted social security numbers or full account numbers on your local drive.
blocks.title: Data Privacy Reminder

blocks.text: The biggest mistake is failing to verify the source of the document. A PDF pay stub can be easily edited. Always compare the company name on the pay stub with the employer listed on the application. If the contact information is missing, ask the applicant for a direct line to their HR department.

Another issue is ignoring the difference between gross and net income. Rental criteria usually rely on gross income. Ensure you are calculating the correct figure before making a decision. If you are using Excel or Google Sheets to track these numbers, ensure your formulas are correct. A simple error here can lead to a bad leasing decision.

faq.question: What documents should I ask for?
faq.answer: Standard practice includes two to four recent pay stubs, a bank statement, and sometimes a W-2 or tax return for self-employed applicants.

faq.question: How do I verify self-employed income?
faq.answer: Request the last two years of tax returns or a profit and loss statement signed by a certified accountant.

faq.question: Can I use AI to help with this?
faq.answer: You can use AI to draft emails to employers for verification, but you should always review the output for accuracy before sending.
